case: SFDC-79904 / nVista 2P — Laser is not turned on (mid-session)
issue: Customer sees 'Laser is not turned on' critical warning mid-session during triggered/BNC-triggered recordings. Also reports 'System is loading' freeze and inverted/displaced image display (~1 in 20 recordings).

log_evidence.hub.log_line_85518: sendErrorNotification: {level:critical, message:'Laser is not turned on', module:record}
log_evidence.hub.log_line_85514: setLaserOn Cannot communicate with Laser (empty Read Frame from laser controller UART)
log_evidence.glitch_pattern: Get Laser status failed with error: Frame size too small → mqttLoopLaser com. glitch or error in getting status
log_evidence.mppc_errors: All mppcResetHandler reset:true calls fail with Internal ErrorCode 0x50

cause: Two-layered issue: (1) A transient UART/serial communication failure between hub_manager and the laser controller causes an empty read frame precisely when a triggered-recording start is attempted, resulting in the false 'Laser is not turned on' notification. (2) Corrupted browser local storage / frontend session state (confirmed by engineering) also contributes to the false notification. Issues 1 and 3 (display artifacts) are known software bugs fixed in the production release.

immediate_workaround: Clear browser cache: Caps Lock ON → Ctrl+Shift+I → Application → Local Storage → 127.0.0.1 → Clear → Ctrl+Shift+R
Or: Session → Edit Session → Reset Session
Or: Press Play button to re-initialize pipeline (re-establishes laser communication)
If notification appears during recording: clear the notification and continue — recording is unaffected
fix.permanent_fix: Upgrade to production software version (issues 1 and 3 are fixed in production build)

agent_diagnosis_accuracy: Partial match. Agent correctly identified: (1) transient UART comm glitch in hub.log, (2) laser hardware physically fine, (3) press Play / reinitialize as workaround, (4) software version issue. Agent missed: browser local storage corruption as a contributing cause, and that engineering confirmed a software-level fix in production.
